Hi, I am Reem

I have been supervising since 2009, and the associates I work best with want more than signed hours. They want to understand what is happening in the room, including what is happening in their own nervous system while a client is falling apart in front of them.

My clinical centre is IFS-informed EMDR: processing that consults the protective parts of a person instead of overriding them. Somatic Experiencing sets the pace, NARM tracks the patterns underneath. That is what I teach, and it is what I practise.

I expect you to show up prepared, be honest, and tell me when something goes wrong. In return you get help building a practice, not just a log.

Why three individual plus one group: Texas requires at least four hours of supervision a month and caps group supervision at half your total hours. Three and one keeps group at a quarter, which leaves margin if a month goes sideways. The rules are laid out in full in the licensure guide.

What supervision here is like

Supervision is not a compliance meeting. It is the place you bring the session that went sideways, the client you think about on the drive home, and the parts of the work that are touching something of your own.

I work collaboratively, which means I expect you to show up prepared, be honest, and tell me when something goes wrong. In return you get someone who will help you build a practice, not just log hours: fee setting, caseload shape, online presence, referral relationships, and the ethics of all of it.

The clinical lens is trauma-informed and body-oriented. We will talk about the nervous system in the room, yours as much as the client's, and about transference and countertransference as information rather than error.

You will probably fit well here if

  • You want developmental trauma and C-PTSD work to be a real part of your training.
  • You are drawn to NARM, Somatic Experiencing, EMDR, IFS-informed work or Brainspotting.
  • You intend to build a private practice, now or eventually.
  • You can tolerate direct feedback and want it.
  • You are curious about experiential and body-based supervision, including work with horses.

LPC supervision questions

How much does LPC supervision cost in Texas with Reem Glasco?

Supervision is $425 a month, which covers three individual supervision hours and one group hour. Associates working inside an agency or group practice can arrange a three-month contract at $500 a month. Optional equine-assisted sessions are $60 each.

How many supervision hours do I get each month?

Four: three individual hours and one group hour, based on a caseload of ten or more clients a week. If your caseload or board requirements differ, raise it in the consult and we will plan the cadence together.

Is supervision online or in person?

Supervision is online only, which means any LPC Associate licensed in Texas can work with Reem regardless of where in the state they live. The optional equine sessions and the annual retreat are the in-person exceptions.

Are there supervision openings right now?

One spot opens in fall 2026 and one in spring 2027. Because supervision is capped deliberately, it is worth booking a consult before a spot opens rather than after.

Do you provide a placement site for supervisees?

Yes, online only. Site verification is part of the application process, so the placement details are confirmed before any agreement is signed.

Does supervision include EMDR consultation?

Yes. Reem is an EMDRIA Approved Consultant and offers free individual EMDR consults to her own associates. Paid consultation toward EMDR certification is available separately to therapists who are not supervisees.

What does Reem expect from a supervisee?

Show up prepared, be honest, and communicate when something goes wrong. Supervision works when the hard material arrives in the room rather than getting managed outside it.

What is equine-assisted supervision?

Optional in-person sessions with horses near Dripping Springs, Texas, at $60 each. Horses respond to what your nervous system is doing rather than what you intend, which makes them an unusually direct teacher of presence and of your own countertransference. Training for therapists working with horses is also available for an additional fee.

Consultation questions

Do these hours count toward EMDR certification?

Reem is an EMDRIA Approved Consultant, which is the credential EMDRIA requires for consultation hours toward certification. Confirm your own current requirements with EMDRIA, since their criteria are set by them and can change.

How much does EMDR consultation cost?

$185 for an individual online hour. LPC Associates under Reem's supervision receive individual EMDR consults at no additional cost.

I am not in Texas. Can we still work together?

Consultation is a peer professional relationship rather than clinical care, so it is not limited to Texas in the way therapy and LPC supervision are. Check what your own licensing board expects of your consultation arrangements.

What if my EMDR training was years ago?

That is common and it is a fine place to start. Bring a case you feel stuck on and we will rebuild confidence from the preparation phases forward rather than starting from the manual.

Ask about the next one

Why any of this, when you already have supervision

Because the thing that limits most clinicians is not knowledge. It is how much they can stay present for before something in them takes over: the urge to fix, to reassure, to change the subject, to work harder than the client.

That capacity does not grow much by talking about it. It grows by being in a situation where your own state is the material, and then noticing what you do. Walking does some of that. Horses do a lot of it.

Mindful trail retreats

An annual retreat for interns, associates and licensed therapists. We walk, and the subject is presence: what it feels like when you have it, what takes it away, and what you do instead when you have lost it.

It is not a conference and there is no curriculum to get through. Expect quiet, movement, small-group work, and more silence than most professional events are comfortable with.

Associates in supervision with Reem are included in the annual retreat. Others are welcome as space allows.

Good fit if

  • You give your clients regulation skills you do not practise yourself.
  • You are competent and quietly exhausted.
  • You want professional development that is not another slide deck.
  • You are curious about somatic work but have only read about it.

Working with horses

Horses respond to what your nervous system is doing, not to what you intend or say. A therapist who is subtly braced gets a different horse than one who is settled, and the feedback arrives in seconds rather than in a supervision session three weeks later.

Two ways in. Associates in supervision can add equine-assisted sessions at $60 each as part of their supervision. Licensed therapists who want to bring horses into their own practice can train with Reem, for a separate fee.

Ethics CEUs for Texas LPCs

Texas LPCs need 24 continuing education hours in each two-year renewal period, including at least 6 hours in ethics, and since January 2024 at least half of the total must come from a provider listed in §681.140(f). Reem offers ethics continuing education periodically.

The full renewal requirements are in the licensure guide, including what LPC-S status adds.

Note for the site build: list the next retreat date, the equine training format and fee, and the next ethics CEU offering with its provider approval, then link a registration route. Until those are set, this page sends people to the contact form.

Questions

Do I have to be Reem's supervisee to attend a retreat?

No. Associates in supervision with Reem are included, and other interns, associates and licensed therapists are welcome as space allows.

How much do the equine sessions cost?

$60 per session for LPC Associates in supervision with Reem, added on to the $425 monthly supervision fee. Training for therapists who want to work with horses in their own practice is priced separately per offering.

Do the ethics CEUs count toward Texas LPC renewal?

Ethics hours count toward the 6-hour ethics requirement inside your 24 hours per renewal period. Because at least half your total hours must come from a provider listed in 22 TAC §681.140(f), always confirm the provider status of any offering, including this one, before you rely on it.

Is any of this therapy?

No. Retreats and training are professional development, and supervision is supervision. If what you need is your own therapy, that is a good thing to want, and Reem can point you to a referral rather than mixing the roles.

Home / Licensure Guide

Getting licensed as an LPC in Texas

Full LPC licensure in Texas requires a qualifying graduate degree, two exams, an LPC Associate licence, and then 3,000 clock-hours of supervised experience under a Council-approved supervisor. At least 1,500 of those hours must be direct client counselling contact, and the 3,000 cannot be completed in fewer than 18 months. While you are accruing them you must receive at least four hours of supervision a month, with no more than half of your total supervision hours in a group. Your LPC Associate licence expires 60 months from issuance and cannot be renewed.

Rules cited below are from 22 Texas Administrative Code, Chapter 681, administered by the Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council. Current as of September 2026. Rules change, so verify anything you are about to rely on against BHEC directly.

The path, in four stages

Each stage has to be complete before the next one counts.
StageWhat it takesRule
Graduate degree 60 semester hours for programs begun on or after 1 August 2017, 48 before that, including a supervised practicum of at least 300 clock-hours with at least 100 hours of direct client counselling, carrying academic credit §681.82, §681.83
Exams The NCE or the NCMHCE, plus the Texas Jurisprudence Exam. Your jurisprudence certificate must be dated no more than six months before your application is received §681.72
LPC Associate licence Apply and be licensed before you begin. Hours worked while unlicensed do not count, in any setting. The licence expires 60 months from issuance and cannot be renewed §681.72, §681.140
Supervised experience 3,000 clock-hours, at least 1,500 of them direct client counselling contact, over no fewer than 18 months, under a Council-approved supervisor §681.92

The hours, and how long they actually take

The 3,000 is rarely the binding constraint. The 1,500 direct hours are, because direct hours accrue only while you are in session with a client. Everything else, notes, admin, training, staffing, counts toward the other 1,500.

Time to reach 1,500 direct hours, before holidays, no-shows and ramp-up.
Direct client hours a weekWeeks to 1,500Roughly
256018 months, held to the floor
207518 months, held to the floor
151002 years
121252 years 5 months
81883 years 7 months

Two things fall out of that table. Above roughly twenty direct hours a week, the 18-month floor decides your timeline, not your caseload, so pushing harder buys you nothing. Below about twelve, the 60-month expiry on your Associate licence starts to become the real deadline, and cancellations and slow referral months eat the margin faster than most associates expect.

The supervision rules associates get wrong

  • Four hours a month is a minimum, not a target. You must receive at least four hours of supervision in every month you are counselling, unless your supervisor approves an extended leave of a month or more in writing.
  • Individual means up to two associates. BHEC defines individual supervision as a supervisor with one or two associates. Three or more is group.
  • No more than half your total hours can be group. Over the whole period, group supervision cannot exceed 50% of your supervision hours. This is why a structure of three individual hours plus one group hour a month works cleanly: group is a quarter of the total.
  • Two supervisors, maximum. You may have up to two LPC supervisors on file at a time, splitting hours by mutual agreement.
  • Paperwork has deadlines. The Supervisory Agreement Form goes in before supervision starts. The Supervised Experience Documentation Form is due within 30 days after supervision ends.
  • Miss the 60 months and you start over. If the required hours are not complete when your Associate licence expires, you reapply and meet whatever requirements are in effect at that time.

How supervision with Reem is structured

Choosing a supervisor

You will spend eighteen months to three years with this person, during the period that shapes how you practise for the rest of your career. Interview them.

Worth asking

  • How many associates are you supervising right now, and what is your cap?
  • What is the fee, what does it include, and does it change if my caseload changes?
  • Is the fee monthly or hourly, and what happens in a month when I only need two hours?
  • How is group supervision structured, and how many people are in it?
  • Are you reachable between sessions when something urgent comes up?
  • What are your clinical models, and are you willing to supervise work outside them?
  • Will you help me build a practice, or only sign hours?
  • How do you give corrective feedback, and can you give me an example?
  • Who employs me, and does that create a conflict with who supervises me?

Reasons to walk away

  • No written supervision agreement.
  • The Supervisory Agreement Form is not filed before you start seeing clients.
  • Hours are not documented contemporaneously, or records are treated as the supervisor's property.
  • Sessions get cancelled and not rescheduled, leaving you short for the month.
  • You cannot get a straight answer about fees.
  • Feedback is only reassurance. If nothing you do is ever questioned, you are paying for a signature.

What supervision costs

Fee structures vary more than the headline number suggests. Some supervisors charge per hour, some charge a flat monthly rate covering the full four hours, and some charge less per hour but exclude group. Agencies sometimes cover supervision entirely, sometimes in exchange for a lower fee split, which is a real cost even when it is not an invoice.

Compare on the monthly total for four compliant hours, not on the hourly rate. Then ask what else is included: EMDR or modality consultation, practice-building help, a placement site, retreats, access between sessions.

For reference, supervision with Reem is $425 a month covering three individual hours and one group hour, or $500 a month on a three-month contract for associates inside an agency. EMDR consultation is included at no cost while you are her associate.

Staying licensed, and becoming a supervisor

Continuing education

Full LPCs complete 24 hours of continuing education in each two-year renewal period, including at least 6 hours in ethics and 3 hours in cultural diversity and competency, plus an HHSC-approved human trafficking prevention course. Since 1 January 2024 at least half of the 24 hours must come from a provider listed in §681.140(f). You also pass the jurisprudence exam each renewal period, which counts as one hour of ethics credit.

Ethics CEUs and training with Reem

Becoming an LPC-S

Supervisor status requires an unrestricted LPC licence in good standing for at least five years, plus either a 40-clock-hour supervision course meeting §681.147 or a for-credit doctoral-level course in supervision. Once approved, holding it requires 6 hours of supervision-specific continuing education per renewal period, which count inside the 24.

BHEC's current guidance says the supervision course does not expire once completed, while the rule text has historically referenced recency windows. If your certificate is old, confirm with BHEC before you apply.

Texas LPC licensure questions

How many supervised hours do you need for an LPC in Texas?

3,000 clock-hours of supervised experience under a Council-approved supervisor, of which at least 1,500 must be direct client counselling contact. Only actual time spent counselling counts as direct. The 3,000 cannot be completed in fewer than 18 months, per 22 TAC §681.92.

How many hours of supervision does an LPC Associate need each month?

A minimum of four hours a month while you are counselling. Individual supervision means a supervisor with one or two associates; group means three or more. No more than 50% of your total supervision hours may be group. You can have up to two LPC supervisors on file at once.

How long does it take to become an LPC in Texas?

Eighteen months at the absolute fastest after you are licensed as an Associate, because that floor applies regardless of how quickly you accrue hours. At fifteen direct client hours a week it takes about two years; at eight a week, closer to three and a half. Add the two to three years of graduate study before that.

Does my LPC Associate licence expire?

Yes. It expires 60 months from the date of issuance and cannot be renewed. If you have not completed the required supervised experience in that window, you must reapply for licensure and meet the requirements in effect at the time of reapplication.

Do hours count if I worked before getting my Associate licence?

No. Hours obtained by an unlicensed person do not count toward the supervised experience requirement, in any setting. Get licensed first.

Can I do supervision online in Texas?

Yes. Texas rules set the amount and structure of supervision rather than requiring it to be in person, and online supervision is common across the state. Reem Glasco, LPC-S, supervises online only, which means associates anywhere in Texas can work with her.

What qualifies someone to supervise LPC Associates in Texas?

An unrestricted Texas LPC licence in good standing for at least five years, plus a 40-clock-hour supervision course meeting 22 TAC §681.147 or a for-credit doctoral-level course in supervision, and approval by BHEC as an LPC-S. Verify any supervisor's status on the BHEC licence lookup before signing an agreement.

Home / Approach

How the methods work, in plain language

Reem's focus is IFS-informed EMDR: EMDR run with parts awareness, so the protective parts of you get consulted rather than overridden. It sits alongside two other approaches. Somatic Experiencing works with the nervous system directly, in small doses, to widen what you can tolerate. NARM works with the patterns that formed in childhood and how they still shape your present. Brainspotting comes in where it helps.

NARM, the NeuroAffective Relational Model

NARM starts from curiosity rather than diagnosis. Where did I learn this pattern? How was it serving me? Is it still?

The invitation is to notice how a pattern keeps you from being present in your own life, and to discover through felt sense which path leads toward thriving. It is less about excavating the past than about meeting what the past installed, now, with attention.

Reem is a NARM therapist and NARM is the spine of most of her work with developmental trauma.

Best when

  • The trouble is a lifelong pattern, not a single event.
  • You understand your history intellectually and nothing has changed.
  • Self-criticism is doing most of the talking.

Somatic Experiencing

Somatic Experiencing, developed by Dr Peter Levine, treats trauma as something the body is still holding rather than a story the mind needs to retell. Sessions track physical sensation and the small movements a threat response never got to finish.

The work is titrated, meaning slow and in doses, because a nervous system that gets flooded learns that attention to the body is dangerous. Done at the right pace, it widens your window of tolerance and your resilience.

Reem is a Somatic Experiencing Practitioner (SEP).

Best when

  • Shock trauma is in the picture: an accident, an assault, a medical event.
  • You go numb, or flood, when you talk about hard things.
  • Anxiety lives in your chest and stomach more than your thoughts.

EMDR

EMDR helps the brain finish processing experiences it stored in raw form. Reem is EMDR certified and an EMDRIA Approved Consultant, trained in ASSYST, PRECI and IGTP-OTS protocols and in IFS-informed EMDR.

Her emphasis is stabilisation first: acute stress, ongoing stress, feeling overwhelmed, loss. Only with that footing does the processing work become useful rather than destabilising.

Therapists seeking consultation on their own EMDR practice can work with Reem as a consultant.

Best when

  • Specific memories intrude, or certain triggers reliably hijack you.
  • You are in an ongoing stressful situation and need footing before insight.
  • Talking about it has stopped helping.

IFS-informed EMDR, where most of the work happens

Standard EMDR asks you to hold a memory and let the processing run. For people with developmental trauma that instruction often meets an internal objection: a part of you that has spent years keeping this material at a distance and has good reasons.

Internal Family Systems gives us language for that. Rather than pushing past the protector, we get to know it. What is it afraid will happen if you go near this? What does it need in place first? Processing starts when the protective parts agree to it, not when the protocol says it is time.

Reem's emphasis is phases one and two, the history-taking and preparation phases, because that is where most stalled EMDR actually stalls. Build enough stability and enough internal agreement there, and the later phases stop being a fight.

She completed steps one through three of IFS-informed EMDR training in 2025, is EMDR certified and an EMDRIA Approved Consultant, and consults with other therapists on exactly this.

What this looks like in session

  • Naming the parts in the room: the one that wants to heal, the one that wants to leave, the one that thinks this is self-indulgent.
  • Unblending, so you can look at a part rather than speak as it.
  • Asking permission from protectors before any target gets processed.
  • Resourcing and stabilisation that a protective part actually trusts.
  • Slowing or pausing processing when a part objects, and treating that objection as information rather than resistance.

Best when

  • EMDR has been tried before and went nowhere, or went badly.
  • You flood, dissociate or go blank when you approach the material.
  • Part of you wants this and part of you really does not.
  • The trauma is developmental and layered rather than a single event.

How the three fit together

They are not three separate treatments you pick between. In practice they interlock: NARM asks what pattern is running and where it was learned, Somatic Experiencing sets the pace your nervous system can hold, and IFS-informed EMDR does the processing once the first two have made room for it.

Which one leads on a given day depends on what you arrive with. A week of acute stress calls for stabilisation. A recurring relational pattern calls for curiosity. A memory that keeps intruding calls for processing, once the parts holding it are on board.

Walking, and horses

Some of this work happens outside. Mindful trail walk therapy puts movement and nature underneath the conversation, which changes what becomes sayable. Equine sessions near Dripping Springs add an animal that responds to your actual state rather than your presented one.

Reem also runs mindful trail retreats for interns, associates and licensed therapists, where the subject is presence and what gets in its way.

Questions about the methods

What is IFS-informed EMDR?

EMDR practised with Internal Family Systems awareness. Before any memory is processed, the protective parts of you that object to the work are identified and consulted, and resourcing is built that those parts trust. It makes EMDR usable for people with developmental trauma, where standard protocol timing often destabilises rather than resolves. Reem Glasco focuses on phases one and two, the preparation phases.

Why not just do standard EMDR?

For a single discrete trauma with a stable nervous system, standard protocol often works well. When trauma is developmental and layered, parts of you have organised around keeping it away, and processing that skips those parts tends to flood, stall or stop working. Consulting them first is slower at the start and faster overall.

Do NARM, Somatic Experiencing and EMDR get used in the same session?

Often, yes. Reem is a NARM therapist, a Somatic Experiencing Practitioner and EMDR certified, so the approaches move with what you bring. NARM tracks the pattern, Somatic Experiencing sets the pacing, IFS-informed EMDR handles processing when there is room for it.

Home / About

Reem Glasco, LPC-S

Reem Glasco is a Licensed Professional Counselor Supervisor in Texas, licence 66562, and has held supervisor status since 2009 with over fifteen years of clinical experience. She is a NARM therapist, a Somatic Experiencing Practitioner (SEP), EMDR certified and an EMDRIA Approved Consultant. She was a Clinical Partner at Capital Area Counseling from 2021 to 2025 and practises from Cedar Park, Texas, working online statewide.

How I work

My NARM approach is an invitation to be curious about your patterns, and about how they keep you from being present in your own life. Where did I learn this? How was it serving me? How does being present give me a choice about which path leads to thriving?

My EMDR work is IFS-informed, which means the protective parts of you get consulted before anything gets processed, and my emphasis is on phases one and two where that agreement is built. It is weighted toward stabilisation: acute stress, ongoing stress, overwhelm, loss. My Somatic Experiencing approach meets shock trauma in a titrated way, slow and gentle, building your window of tolerance rather than testing it.

I teach effortless self care through walk and mindful therapy, and I run mindful trail retreats for interns, associates and therapists, where we explore being present and what gets in the way of it.

I am also an LPC supervisor. Supervision is online, and I offer mindful retreats for associate therapists to expand their personal and professional awareness in the field.

You can also find me on Psychology Today.

Texas notices

Licensing and complaints

Reem Glasco holds Texas LPC licence number 66562. To file a complaint about a Texas licensee, contact the Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council at 1-800-821-3205 or enforcement@bhec.texas.gov to request the appropriate form. Mailed complaints go to:

Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council
Attn: Enforcement Division
George H. W. Bush State Office Building
1801 Congress Ave, Ste 7.300
Austin, TX 78701

The Executive Council investigates and prosecutes professional misconduct by marriage and family therapists, professional counselors, psychologists, psychological associates, social workers and licensed specialists in school psychology. Not every complaint or dispute involves professional misconduct, and the Council will explain how to file either way. Licence verification is available at bhec.texas.gov.

Access to your records

Under the Texas Medical Records Privacy Act (HB 4224, effective 1 September 2025) you have the right to access your health care records and to file complaints. Submit a written request to info@findingbalancecounselingpllc.com. Records are provided electronically within 15 business days unless you agree to another format or an exception applies.

Complaints about this practice

To raise a concern directly, email info@findingbalancecounselingpllc.com. To file a consumer complaint with the state, forms and instructions are on the licensing authority's website and, where applicable, the Texas Attorney General's site.

Home / FAQ

Questions people ask first

Short version: LPC supervision is $425 a month for three individual hours and one group hour, online statewide. EMDR consultation is $185 an hour with an EMDRIA Approved Consultant. Therapy is $240 for a 50-minute online session with Reem, or less with the practice's associates. Everything starts with a free consult. The practice is in Cedar Park, Texas, with in-person trail and equine options near Austin for adults.

Getting started

How do I become a client?

Email the practice to request a free 15-minute consult. If it is a fit, you receive client forms and we schedule. If it is not, you get a referral rather than a polite brush-off.

Where is Finding Balance Counseling located?

The practice is based in Cedar Park, Texas, and works online with clients anywhere in the state, including Austin. In-person trail walk sessions happen outdoors in central Texas, and equine sessions are near Dripping Springs.

Should I see Reem or one of the associates?

Usually it comes down to availability and fee. Reem keeps a small therapy caseload alongside her supervision and consultation work, at $240 a session. The LPC Associates she supervises have more open calendars and lower fees, including sliding scale, and practise under her supervision.

Who does Reem work with?

Young adults, college-age clients and individual adults, plus LPC Associates and licensed therapists in supervision or consultation. The practice does not work with young children.

What are the office hours?

By appointment. Walk and table therapy sessions are on Fridays.

Money

How much is a session?

$240 for a 50-minute online session, private pay. Trail walk and movement sessions run $240 to $370 depending on length. Sliding-scale fees are available through the practice's LPC Associates.

Do you accept insurance?

Sessions are private pay and the practice is not accepting new Blue Cross Blue Shield clients. Payment is by major credit card.

What is the cancellation policy?

Cancel telehealth appointments at least 24 hours ahead, or an $85 fee may apply. In-person walk therapy is paid in advance and is non-refundable inside 48 hours.

The work itself

What kind of therapy does Reem practise?

NARM for the patterns formed early in life, Somatic Experiencing for what the nervous system is still holding, and EMDR for specific traumatic material once there is enough stability. IFS-informed and Brainspotting elements are used where parts of a person disagree about the work.

What is walk and talk therapy?

A therapy session held outdoors while walking, with nature and movement underneath the conversation. It runs 75 minutes to two hours, is for adults only, and requires a consult plus one to three online sessions first. Fees are $240 to $370, paid in advance.

Do you work with horses?

Yes. Equine-assisted sessions are available near Dripping Springs, Texas, for clients, for LPC associates in supervision at $60 a session, and as optional training for therapists who want to work with horses themselves.

For therapists

How many supervised hours do I need for a Texas LPC?

3,000 clock-hours under a Council-approved supervisor, at least 1,500 of them direct client counselling contact, over no fewer than 18 months, with a minimum of four supervision hours a month and no more than half of your total supervision hours in a group. The licensure guide on this site works through all of it, including the 60-month expiry on your Associate licence.

Do you run retreats or training for therapists?

Yes. An annual mindful trail retreat for interns, associates and licensed therapists, equine-assisted sessions and training near Dripping Springs, and periodic ethics continuing education for Texas LPCs. Associates in supervision with Reem are included in the annual retreat.

Are you accepting LPC Associates for supervision?

One supervision spot opens in fall 2026 and one in spring 2027. Supervision is $425 a month for three individual hours and one group hour, online and statewide in Texas. Applications start with a free 30-minute consult.

Can my agency contract supervision for a short period?

Yes. Three-month contracts are available for associates working within an agency or group practice at $500 a month.

Can you be my EMDR consultant?

Reem is an EMDRIA Approved Consultant. Individual consultation is $185 an hour online, focused on IFS-informed EMDR for phases one and two, and it is free for her own LPC associates.

Do you offer ethics CEUs?

Ethics continuing education for Texas LPCs is offered periodically. Email the practice to ask about the next session.

Safety

What if I am in crisis right now?

This practice does not provide emergency care. Call or text 988 for the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, or call 911 if you are in immediate danger. Reach out here once you are safe and we can talk about ongoing support.

Still deciding?

A consult costs nothing and commits you to nothing.

Home / Therapy

Therapy at Finding Balance

Reem Glasco, LPC-S, sees a small number of adults and young adults for developmental trauma, C-PTSD, anxiety, panic attacks, depression, procrastination and life transitions. Sessions are 50 minutes at $240, online anywhere in Texas, private pay. Because her caseload is limited by her supervision and consultation work, most new clients are seen by the practice's LPC Associates, who have openings including at sliding-scale fees. Trail walk sessions are available in person in central Texas for adults at $240 to $370.

Request a free 15-minute consult See fees

What people bring here

  • Developmental trauma: patterns that formed early, before you had words or choices.
  • C-PTSD and PTSD, including trauma that is ongoing rather than finished.
  • Anxiety, panic attacks, and a body that stays braced when nothing is happening.
  • Depression, flatness, and a sense that something is off you cannot point at.
  • Procrastination that is not laziness and does not respond to discipline.
  • Life transitions: graduating, leaving, arriving, becoming a parent, losing someone.
  • Self care for mothers, which usually starts with permission.

Who this is for

Adults and young adults, including college-age clients. The practice does not work with young children.

Trail walk, movement and equine sessions are for adults only, and need a consult plus one to three online sessions first, so we know each other before we are outside.

How IFS-informed EMDR, Somatic Experiencing and NARM fit together

Reem, or one of the associates?

Both are options, and the honest answer is usually availability. Reem holds a small caseload alongside supervising associates and consulting on EMDR. The associates she supervises are earlier in their careers, working under her supervision, with lower fees and more open calendars.

Working with Reem

$240 for 50 minutes, private pay, online across Texas. Limited openings. Best fit for complex developmental trauma and stalled EMDR.

Working with an associate

Lower fees, including sliding scale, and sooner availability. Supervised by Reem, so the clinical approach is the same lineage.

Common questions about therapy here

How much does a therapy session cost?

$240 for a 50-minute online session with Reem, private pay. Trail walk and movement sessions are $240 to $370 depending on length. The practice's LPC Associates see clients at lower fees, including sliding scale.

Do you take insurance?

The practice is private pay and is not accepting new Blue Cross Blue Shield clients. Payment is by major credit card. If you plan to seek out-of-network reimbursement, raise it in the consult so you know what documentation to expect.

Is therapy in person or online?

Online across Texas is the default. In person means trail walk and movement therapy on Fridays, or equine sessions near Dripping Springs, both for adults, both after a consult and one to three online sessions.

What happens in a first session?

Mostly orientation: what brought you, what you want different, what your nervous system does under stress, and how we will pace the work. Nothing about trauma gets opened faster than you can stay present for.

How long will therapy take?

It depends what we are working with. Stabilisation can be a handful of sessions. Developmental trauma is slower, because we are building capacity rather than processing a single event. We review it together instead of guessing at the start.

What if I need help sooner than you have openings?

Ask about the associates, who generally have availability sooner and lower fees. If neither fits, Reem will refer you out rather than leave you on a waitlist. If you are in crisis, call or text 988.
